{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
    "line": 65,
    "severity": "critical",
    "category": "security",
    "title": "V2 canManage() grants group-management privileges to VIEW-only admins",
    "body": "GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-argument) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, so an admin who only has the `view` scope on the 'Groups' all-resource is treated as if they can manage groups. This affects every admin endpoint guarded by `auth.groups().requireManage()` without a specific group argument, in particular GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups) and the manage-only branches of GroupResource (updateGroup, deleteGroup, addChild, role-mappings). A user policy that grants only `view` on the `Groups` resource type now lets the holder create, rename, delete and reassign top-level groups, violating least privilege. The interface javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() even codifies this behavior. V1's canManage() correctly limits itself to the `manage-users` admin role; the V2 override should match that and check only `MANAGE` (or equivalently delegate to a per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` over an all-groups resource)."
  },
  {
    "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
    "line": 121,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource.getId() instead of resource.getName()",
    "body": "Inside `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` the iteration is `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> { hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...); granted.add(groupResource.getId()); })`. In the V2 schema, per-group resources are created with `name == groupId` (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup / getOrCreateResource), so `groupResource.getId()` is the resource's own auto-generated UUID, not the group's id. Two concrete consequences: (a) `hasPermission` calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupResource.getId())` which never matches the per-group resource, so every per-group permission check falls back to the all-groups evaluation and ignores scope restrictions on the specific group; (b) the returned set is populated with resource UUIDs that the user search interprets as group ids (see UsersResource.searchForUser where the set is set as `UserModel.GROUPS`), so the user filter ends up matching no real groups and the entire view-by-group filter is broken. Both `getId()` calls should be `getName()` to mirror the V1 implementation that used `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`."
  },
  {
    "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java",
    "line": 144,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null",
    "body": "In `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, when no per-group resource is found, the code does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` followed immediately by `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can legitimately return null (it returns null whenever `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false, when the resourceType argument is null, when the schema type is unknown, or when the 'Groups' resource has not yet been persisted in the resource store). Passing that null into `findByResource(server, null)` will NPE, crashing the admin REST call. Guard the lookup with a null check, mirroring the equivalent code in UserPermissionsV2 which has the same defect."
  },
  {
    "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java",
    "line": 109,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null",
    "body": "`hasPermission(UserModel user, ...)` performs the same fallback as GroupPermissionsV2: `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE); if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`. When `getResourceTypeResource` returns null (feature disabled, schema not yet initialized, or 'Users' resource missing), `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` throws a NullPointerException. This affects every V2 canView/canManage/canImpersonate/canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership call path. Add a null guard before `findByResource`."
  },
  {
    "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java",
    "line": 47,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "security",
    "title": "Removed AdminRoles.ADMIN fallback may deny master-realm admins under FGAP V2",
    "body": "The pre-existing V2 overrides for canView(UserModel), canManage(UserModel), canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership used to short-circuit on `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, ...)`. The new versions drop the `AdminRoles.ADMIN` role entirely. With AdminPermissionsEnabled + ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 on a child realm, a master-realm administrator holding only the `admin` role (no `manage-users`/`view-users` client role) will no longer satisfy the role check, and only the Authz policy engine will be consulted. Unless the realm admin has explicitly created a UserPolicy mapping the admin user to the 'Users' resource, every user-management call will fail with 403. This is a behavioral regression relative to V1 and the previous V2 implementation; either keep the ADMIN check or document/guarantee that ADMIN implies these scopes via policy."
  },
  {
    "file": "tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java",
    "line": 68,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "test_gap",
    "title": "Missing test that VIEW on Groups does not imply manage privileges",
    "body": "GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest grants a `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type in `testViewGroups` but only exercises the list endpoint. There is no test that asserts a VIEW-only admin cannot create, update, delete groups or add child groups. Given the canManage() privilege escalation introduced in GroupPermissionsV2 (see security finding), a regression test should be added that grants only VIEW scope and expects 403 on POST /groups, PUT /groups/{id}, DELETE /groups/{id}, and POST /groups/{id}/children. Without it the escalation can re-recur unnoticed."
  },
  {
    "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java",
    "line": 88,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "doc_defect",
    "title": "canManage() javadoc misrepresents required scopes",
    "body": "The javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` says \"Or if it has a permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` or `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` groups\". That text legitimizes the privilege-escalation behavior implemented in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (a viewer should not be a manager). The doc should match V1 semantics: only `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` (or the `manage-users` admin role) grants manage; `view` should not."
  }
]}

findings.title: V2 canManage() grants group-management privileges to VIEW-only admins
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-argument) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, so an admin who only has the `view` scope on the 'Groups' all-resource is treated as if they can manage groups. This affects every admin endpoint guarded by `auth.groups().requireManage()` without a specific group argument, in particular GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups) and the manage-only branches of GroupResource (updateGroup, deleteGroup, addChild, role-mappings). A user policy that grants only `view` on the `Groups` resource type now lets the holder create, rename, delete and reassign top-level groups, violating least privilege. The interface javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() even codifies this behavior. V1's canManage() correctly limits itself to the `manage-users` admin role; the V2 override should match that and check only `MANAGE` (or equivalently delegate to a per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` over an all-groups resource).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource.getId() instead of resource.getName()
findings.body: Inside `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` the iteration is `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> { hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...); granted.add(groupResource.getId()); })`. In the V2 schema, per-group resources are created with `name == groupId` (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup / getOrCreateResource), so `groupResource.getId()` is the resource's own auto-generated UUID, not the group's id. Two concrete consequences: (a) `hasPermission` calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupResource.getId())` which never matches the per-group resource, so every per-group permission check falls back to the all-groups evaluation and ignores scope restrictions on the specific group; (b) the returned set is populated with resource UUIDs that the user search interprets as group ids (see UsersResource.searchForUser where the set is set as `UserModel.GROUPS`), so the user filter ends up matching no real groups and the entire view-by-group filter is broken. Both `getId()` calls should be `getName()` to mirror the V1 implementation that used `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`.

findings.title: NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null
findings.body: In `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, when no per-group resource is found, the code does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` followed immediately by `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can legitimately return null (it returns null whenever `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false, when the resourceType argument is null, when the schema type is unknown, or when the 'Groups' resource has not yet been persisted in the resource store). Passing that null into `findByResource(server, null)` will NPE, crashing the admin REST call. Guard the lookup with a null check, mirroring the equivalent code in UserPermissionsV2 which has the same defect.

findings.title: NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null
findings.body: `hasPermission(UserModel user, ...)` performs the same fallback as GroupPermissionsV2: `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE); if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`. When `getResourceTypeResource` returns null (feature disabled, schema not yet initialized, or 'Users' resource missing), `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` throws a NullPointerException. This affects every V2 canView/canManage/canImpersonate/canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership call path. Add a null guard before `findByResource`.

findings.title: Removed AdminRoles.ADMIN fallback may deny master-realm admins under FGAP V2
findings.body: The pre-existing V2 overrides for canView(UserModel), canManage(UserModel), canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership used to short-circuit on `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, ...)`. The new versions drop the `AdminRoles.ADMIN` role entirely. With AdminPermissionsEnabled + ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 on a child realm, a master-realm administrator holding only the `admin` role (no `manage-users`/`view-users` client role) will no longer satisfy the role check, and only the Authz policy engine will be consulted. Unless the realm admin has explicitly created a UserPolicy mapping the admin user to the 'Users' resource, every user-management call will fail with 403. This is a behavioral regression relative to V1 and the previous V2 implementation; either keep the ADMIN check or document/guarantee that ADMIN implies these scopes via policy.

findings.title: Missing test that VIEW on Groups does not imply manage privileges
findings.body: GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest grants a `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type in `testViewGroups` but only exercises the list endpoint. There is no test that asserts a VIEW-only admin cannot create, update, delete groups or add child groups. Given the canManage() privilege escalation introduced in GroupPermissionsV2 (see security finding), a regression test should be added that grants only VIEW scope and expects 403 on POST /groups, PUT /groups/{id}, DELETE /groups/{id}, and POST /groups/{id}/children. Without it the escalation can re-recur unnoticed.

findings.title: canManage() javadoc misrepresents required scopes
findings.body: The javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` says "Or if it has a permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` or `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` groups". That text legitimizes the privilege-escalation behavior implemented in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (a viewer should not be a manager). The doc should match V1 semantics: only `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` (or the `manage-users` admin role) grants manage; `view` should not.
